cases.note: logic_op/precedence: `not x or y` parses as `(not x) or y`
modules:
package test
import future.keywords.or

# x=true, y=true:
# `(not x) or y` = false or true = true -> p=true
# `not (x or y)` = not true = false -> undefined
p if {
  not input.x or input.y
}

cases.note: logic_op/precedence: `x or y and z` parses as `x or (y and z)`
modules:
package test
import future.keywords.and
import future.keywords.or

# x=true, y=false, z=false:
# `x or (y and z)` = true or _ = true -> p=true (short-circuit)
# `(x or y) and z` = (true or false) and false = false -> undefined
p if {
  input.x or input.y and input.z
}

cases.note: logic_op/precedence: `x and y or z and w` parses as `(x and y) or (z and w)`
modules:
package test
import future.keywords.and
import future.keywords.or

# x=false, y=true, z=true, w=true:
# `(x and y) or (z and w)` = false or true = true -> p=true
# `x and (y or z) and w`   = false and ... = false -> undefined
p if {
  input.x and input.y or input.z and input.w
}

cases.note: logic_op/precedence: `not x and not y or z` parses as `((not x) and (not y)) or z`
modules:
package test
import future.keywords.and
import future.keywords.or

# x=true, y=true, z=true:
# `((not x) and (not y)) or z` = (false and false) or true = true -> p=true
# `not x and not (y or z)`     = false and not true = false -> undefined
p if {
  not input.x and not input.y or input.z
}
